value.title: embed-split — chunked embeddings + input hygiene
value.summary: Oversize inputs embed as N overlapping chunk vectors instead of a truncated prefix, and provider batches are hygienic by construction (no empty/whitespace inputs ever reach a provider). Closes backlog rows 68 and 87 under live-measured incident receipts.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Two defects, one pipeline, measured in prod on 2026-08-30 under conversation-ingest load. (1) TRUNCATION: the 2026-08-27 ruling ('truncate now, split later') embeds only a prefix of any input over the model's per-input cap (8192 tokens); conversation turns (20KB+ tool dumps) hit this constantly, so each such turn's TAIL is semantically unsearchable. 'Later' is now: split oversize inputs into overlapping chunks, each with its own vector, grandfathering every existing vector as chunk 0. (2) POISON BATCHES: empty-bodied turns (raw_hash e3b0c442... — the empty-string sha) become embed jobs whose empty text reaches Azure and rejects the WHOLE merged call — measured: one empty turn rejected 530 innocent texts; three poison turns cost 9 rejected calls / 1,639 texts collateral in one wave, and the failed rows revive at every boot sweep (we now bounce on every merge). Filter at mint AND at batch assembly. Prior art both sides: fs2's content-type-aware chunker (ChunkItem(node_id, chunk_index, text), code=400/docs=800/smart=8000 token targets, line-span tracking) and fs3's own dedupe-by-element ranking which ALREADY collapses multiple vectors (raw+smart) per element — chunks widen 2 to N with no ranking redesign.

sections.name: goals
value: Every byte of an oversize input is semantically searchable: N overlapping chunk vectors per (source_hash, kind), not a truncated prefix.
No empty or whitespace-only input ever reaches a provider: filtered at job mint (turn/element enrichment enqueue) AND asserted at batch assembly (defense in depth).
Existing vectors are grandfathered as chunk_no=0 — zero re-embedding, zero backfill cost on migration.
Existing poison rows are healed: empty-input embed jobs are terminally retired (not boot-sweep-revived), with a receipt of how many.
Search behaviour is unchanged for single-chunk content and strictly better for chunked content (the tail can now match); ranking still returns ONE row per element via the existing dedupe.

sections.name: non_goals
value: No change to the 8192-token per-input cap itself or to provider adapters' wire shapes.
No content-type-aware chunk SIZING in v1 (fs2's code=400/docs=800 refinement is a named future; v1 uses one near-cap window size + overlap for all kinds).
No re-embedding of existing truncated rows (the truncated=true inventory is a cheap later backfill, explicitly deferred).
No summarize-lane changes; no ranking algorithm changes beyond consuming N chunk rows through the existing element dedupe.
No queue/lane redesign — this rides the existing embed lane, batch planner, and token-budget splitting untouched.

value.claim: A synthetic input over the per-input cap produces the step-formula chunk count — 1 + ceil((len - window) / (window - overlap)) for len > window, which equals ceil(len/window) only at overlap=0 — with the configured overlap, all sharing (source_hash, source_kind, model_key) and distinct chunk_no; migration proves existing rows read back as chunk_no=0 with no re-embed jobs minted. [Arithmetic corrected 2026-08-30: original ceil(len/window) promise was wrong for positive overlap — u2's implementation ruled authoritative, prose follows the code's math.]
value.receipt: Composed sha 3387d76. Migration 0022_embed_chunks.sql (renumbered from 0021 after conv-readback took that ordinal on main) adds chunk_no SMALLINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 and the exact PK (source_hash, source_kind, chunk_no, model_key). Proven by crates/store/tests/pg_migrations.rs: the catalog PK/type/default assertion, and migration_0022_grandfathers_vectors_without_minting_embed_jobs which applies 1..=21, inserts under the OLD triple key, applies 22..=22, and asserts the row reads back chunk_no=0 with jobs_after == jobs_before (no re-embed minted). 8/8 green on the composed tree. Chunk COUNT arithmetic corrected during the run: with a positive overlap the count is 1 + ceil((len-window)/(window-overlap)), not ceil(len/window) — u2 proved the original prose wrong and o-prime amended it; the implementation asserts the step-based counts.

value.claim: A phrase living ONLY in the tail (beyond the old truncation point) of an oversize document/turn is retrieved by semantic search and resolves to the owning element/turn — mutation-checked: with chunking disabled the same fixture fails.
value.receipt: Tail retrieval proven twice at two levels. Store level, mutation-checked control (crates/store/tests/pg_store_flows.rs): the positive fixture seeds all chunk vectors for a whale, the negative control seeds ONLY its chunk-0 prefix vector, and the tail-only phrase resolves in the positive and returns 0 rows in the control — removing the positive fixture's tail chunk fails it with 0 rows instead of 1. The control is seeded rather than achieved by mutating u2's code, so it reproduces at this sha for the reviewer. Live level: crates/daemon/tests/embed_split.rs drives real intake -> queue drain -> chunking -> search and resolves the tail anchor to conv:9fca61cc-2c7a-4d9d-93eb-1dc92ba69b55#t1. 17/17 store and 1/1 daemon green on the composed tree.

value.claim: Search returns at most one result row per element regardless of how many of its chunk vectors matched, with the best chunk's score, AND a whale element with N matching chunks does not crowd other elements out of a k-limited result set (the caller's LIMIT applies to ELEMENTS, not vectors). Proven by a two-leg fixture: (a) one-row-per-element/best-score, (b) crowd-out — both legs mutation-checked against the collapse removed. [Amended 2026-08-30 by o-prime ruling on PM stop-and-ask: no prior element collapse exists in the read path — u3 ADDS it; the collapse incidentally also closes the pre-existing raw+smart duplicate-hit defect, noted as side-benefit, not claimed scope.]
value.receipt: Both legs green and both mutation-checked. The collapse is added INSIDE the store's nearest CTE (DISTINCT ON (element_id) over a bounded candidate scan in crates/store/src/embeddings.rs, in BOTH query_embeddings and search_elements); the caller's LIMIT is applied to ELEMENTS after collapse. Leg (a) one row per element at the best chunk's score; leg (b) whale crowd-out — a whale seeded with 13 chunks, deliberately exceeding LIMIT 3's initial 12-vector candidate cap, does not displace other elements. Mutation receipt: removing DISTINCT ON (element_id) from both queries fails leg (a) with 3 rows instead of 1 and fails leg (b) with all three returned addresses equal to whale chunks and the other elements crowded out; restored, 17/17 green. Candidate policy audited by the PM rather than accepted on description: 4x initial multiplier, 2x growth, max 8 expansions, returning early when the corpus is exhausted (scanned < candidate_limit) and refusing only on a saturated under-fill — an explicit refusal over a silently under-filled page (tenet 14), reachable only at ~1000+ chunks on a single element. FROZEN SEAM HELD: crates/daemon/src/search.rs has NO diff from u3 (git diff b53428f..HEAD -- crates/daemon/src/search.rs is empty; the 153 lines that differ from the pre-merge base came from main's #80/#84, not this plan).

value.claim: An empty or whitespace-only turn/element body mints NO embed job (proven at the enqueue layer), and a hand-inserted empty job is dropped at batch assembly with a WARN naming the source_hash — the provider call proceeds for the rest of the batch (no collateral rejection). Mutation-checked both layers.
value.receipt: TRUE on the COMPOSED artifact, re-derived by the PM rather than relayed — the coder's receipts only ever proved the coder's worktree. Mint layer: crates/daemon/src/enrich.rs embedding_text_is_nonblank (trim-based) applied at the tree mint, the turn mint (which previously had NO check at all), and both smart-summary mints. Assembly layer: crates/daemon/src/batch.rs:100-109 drops empty/whitespace items after deserialization with a WARN naming source_hash, keeping an empty batch shell so an all-poison job settles without a provider call. INDEPENDENCE PROVEN BY TWO SEPARATE MUTATIONS ON THE MERGED TREE: (1) neutering the mint predicate reds exactly whitespace_turn_mints_no_embed_item_while_its_batchmate_does at embed_batch.rs:142 while the assembly unit tests stay green (9 passed); (2) deleting the assembly retain reds exactly blank_items_are_removed_while_every_batchmate_survives and an_all_blank_job_still_returns_a_batch_shell_for_settlement while the queue-backed mint test stays green (5 passed). Two layers failing for two reasons, not one layer wearing two hats. Restored and re-green after each. VERIFIED SEPARATELY (o-prime row-100 question): the predicate keys on PREPARED text, not body — Turn::canonical (crates/core/src/conversation.rs:233-244, :294-303) renders trimmed body PLUS every item block and :261-269 passes it as Element.raw_text, so a body-empty tool-call turn is RETAINED. Row 105 closed no-dispatch.

value.claim: The heal path terminally retires existing empty-input failed jobs so a daemon boot sweep does NOT revive them, with a count receipt; a post-heal boot proves zero empty-input provider rejections in the log.
value.receipt: Heal implemented, WIRED, and the wiring itself mutation-checked — this AC nearly shipped as a green, tested, unreachable function. fs3_store::retire_empty_embed_jobs (crates/store/src/jobs.rs) inspects payload->'items' TEXT with trim semantics matching the mint filter, refuses malformed or zero-item payloads rather than guessing, narrows to state='failed' AND NOT terminal AND kind='embed', sets terminal=true, and returns the count. It keys on CONTENT emptiness, never on the shared empty-string hash e3b0c442. The gate caught in 19s that nothing called it (E0425, missing re-export); the PM added the re-export and extracted boot's recovery into boot::recover_enrichment_jobs, which retires BEFORE fs3_store::requeue_failed can revive. Trigger proven by crates/daemon/tests/boot_recovery.rs: a poison job and a whitespace job end failed+terminal while a CONTROL job with real text is revived to pending — without that control, a recovery that did nothing at all would pass every assertion. ORDER mutation-checked: swapping the two calls makes the poison return as ('pending', false) and reds both tests; restored, green. A second test proves a second boot does not resurrect what the first retired.

value.claim: Live proof on an isolated daemon: ingest a fixture conversation containing (a) a 25KB turn and (b) an empty agent/system turn — the whale turn is fully searchable including its tail, the empty turn costs zero provider traffic, and the run log shows zero 'input cannot be an empty string' and zero per-input-cap WARNs.
value.receipt: Live proof green: crates/daemon/tests/embed_split.rs, 1/1 on the composed tree. An in-process daemon router on an ephemeral port (127.0.0.1:0) against a disposable FreshDatabase, with a capped injected FakeEmbedder; a fixture conversation carrying a ~25KB turn and an empty turn goes through real intake and queue drain. The whale is fully searchable including its tail; every text the provider RECEIVED is asserted non-empty and under the 8192-token cap (asserted on what arrived, not inferred from an absent error); captured logs contain neither the empty-input rejection nor the legacy per-input-cap prefix WARN. DISCLOSED PROOF GAP, named rather than papered over: this shape does not exercise BINARY BOOT CONFIGURATION, because FakeEmbedder records calls in process memory and a spawned `sealed(...) daemon` child cannot expose them — and 'the empty turn costs zero provider traffic' is checkable only by observing what the provider received. o-prime ratified shape (a) and ruled the binary-boot leg covered elsewhere by design: every merge bounces prod, and ac-0007's post-merge krill observation watches the real binary under real ingest load. Production daemon :7373 was never touched by any test or seat this run.

value.claim: harness checks green in the plan worktree; conventional commits; PR into main; the queue-waste live monitor (krill) observes the next real ingest wave post-merge with zero poison alerts.
value.receipt: PR-side closed by the PM; the post-merge observation leg is o-prime's and krill's by agreement, not claimed here. Closed: `harness checks` GREEN 11/11 on the composed branch at 3387d76 (docs, lock, testdb, checks-contract, daemon-bounce-contract, fmt, clippy, prodguard:before, test, prodguard:after, arch), 4m53s — the third of three gates this session, after an attributable baseline-before-anything green and a u1+main green, so no red could be inherited. Conventional commits throughout (feat/fix/docs/merge), every commit made with `harness commit`; all are direct-verified with a refs/notes/ai entry landed EXCEPT f079a398422c (a docs render rebuild) which returned DEGRADED with no buffer to replay, so that one commit's authorship is unrecorded — reported rather than passed off as green. ONE PR into main; the PM does not merge it. OPEN AND OWNED BY O-PRIME/KRILL: the queue-waste live monitor observing the next real ingest wave post-merge with zero poison alerts, plus the binary-boot leg inherited from ac-0006 via the merge bounce.

value.title: Phase 1: chunked embeddings + input hygiene
value.brief: Single-phase plan, three composable units per the impl-guide: (u1) store/migration — chunk_no in the vector key, grandfather existing rows, heal empty-poison jobs; (u2) enrich/writer — hygiene filter at mint + batch assembly, chunk windowing with overlap replacing prefix truncation; (u3) search/read — N-chunk dedupe generalization + fixtures incl. the tail-retrieval anchor. Composition + review per packet-reviewer.
value.receipt: All three units landed and composed on 009-embed-split at 3387d7612816d87dec9b95bce2ca29c54dbfa02a; harness checks green 11/11; ac-0001..0006 closed with evidence, ac-0007 closed PR-side with its post-merge observation leg handed to o-prime/krill.
